Feluda.description: The main detective, known for his intelligence and wide range of knowledge, whose real name is Pradosh Mitter.

Jatayu.description: A companion and friend of Feluda and a writer of popular crime thrillers whose real name is Lalmohan Ganguli.

Nikhil Burman.description: Someshwar Burman's younger son, currently residing with him, who approaches Feluda for help regarding his father's manuscript on Indian magic.

Someshwar Burman.description: A retired magician and head of the household, father of Akhil and Nikhil Burman, known for performing Indian magic in princely states.

Surya Kumar.description: A magician performing in Calcutta known for his hypnotism act, who is later revealed to be Someshwar Burman's son, Akhil Burman, in disguise.

Srinath.description: A domestic helper who brings tea to Feluda and his friends.

Calcutta.description: A major city in India, now known as Kolkata, where the story is set.

Gorpar.description: A locality in Calcutta, mentioned as the place where Lalmohan Babu lives.

Ambassador.description: A classic Indian car model, popular in the mid-20th century.

Indian magic.description: Traditional forms of magic and illusion practiced in India, often performed in informal settings.

princely states.description: Semi-autonomous regions in pre-independence India ruled by local monarchs, known as rajas.

rajas.description: Traditional Indian monarchs or princes who ruled princely states.

Babu.description: A respectful term of address for men in Bengal, often used after a person's name.

sandesh.description: A traditional Bengali sweet made from fresh cheese and sugar.

Baba.description: A Bengali and Hindi term for father, used affectionately.

Pranavesh Roy.description: Someshwar Burman's secretary, trusted with personal matters and typing the manuscript, who has been working for him for five years and lives in the same house.

Animesh Sen.description: A long-time friend and resident in Someshwar Burman's house, formerly an astrologer, who has read and praised the manuscript and is considered but ruled out as a suspect.

Ranen Tarafdar.description: An artist staying at the Burman house to draw Someshwar Burman's portrait.

Rammohan Roy Sarani.description: A street in Calcutta where Someshwar Burman's house is located.

East Bengal.description: A region in eastern Bengal, now part of Bangladesh, where Someshwar Burman's family originated.

Allahabad.description: A city in northern India, mentioned as the place where Someshwar Burman saw a magician perform.

Indian.description: Refers to things pertaining to India, such as Indian magic.

Krishna.description: A Hindu deity, depicted here as a statue with a flute and adorned with gems.

Raja Dayal Singh.description: A royal figure from Raghunathpur who gifted the Krishna statue to Someshwar Burman.

Raghunathpur.description: A place associated with Raja Dayal Singh, who gave a valuable statue to Someshwar Burman.

Germany.description: A country in Europe where Akhil, Someshwar Burman's elder son, went to work.

Europe.description: The continent where Germany is located and where Akhil is presumed to be.

zamindars.description: Landowners, often hereditary, who collected taxes from peasants in pre-independence India.

homoeopath.description: A practitioner of homeopathy, an alternative medicine system popular in India.

tantrik.description: A practitioner of tantra, a set of esoteric spiritual practices in Hinduism and Buddhism.

chowkidar.description: A watchman or security guard, especially for a house or compound.

veranda.description: A roofed platform along the outside of a house, common in Indian architecture.

Nakshatra Sen.description: A magician who was Surya Kumar's mentor and died on stage.

Maruti.description: An Indian automobile brand; Surya Kumar arrives in a Maruti car.

Japan.description: A country in East Asia, mentioned as a place Surya Kumar has visited for his shows.

Hong Kong.description: A city and special administrative region in China, also visited by Surya Kumar.

Singapore.description: A Southeast Asian city-state, where Surya Kumar has an invitation for a future show.

Patna.description: A city in the Indian state of Bihar, mentioned as Surya Kumar's next destination.

paraphernalia.description: Miscellaneous articles, especially the equipment needed for a particular activity, here referring to a magician's tools.

Avinash.description: Someshwar Burman's oldest servant, who is murdered during the theft of the statue of Krishna.

Inspector Ghosh.description: The police inspector in charge of the case, familiar with Feluda's reputation.

Mirza Ghalib Street.description: A street in Kolkata, India, known for its commercial establishments.

The Modern Sales Bureau.description: The auction house owned by Nikhil Burman, located on Mirza Ghalib Street.

bearer.description: A term used in India for a domestic servant, especially one who serves food or attends to guests.

Bhowanipore.description: A neighborhood in Kolkata (Calcutta), India, where Pranavesh Babu owns a house.

Paris.description: The capital city of France, where Ranen Tarafdar trained as an artist.

Government College of Art.description: A prestigious art institution in Calcutta (Kolkata), India, where Ranen Tarafdar studied.

Gopchand.description: A thief recently released from prison, initially suspected by the police but dismissed by Feluda.

auction house.description: A business establishment where goods, such as antiques or art, are sold to the highest bidder.
